issue.body:
Using the code on `master` (as of https://github.com/eslint/eslint/commit/1c70834295b064021e6aa6698473375063bffbae), I get a false positive with the `indent` rule enabled.

Code:

``` js
while (1 < 2) console.log('hi')
```

Rule:

```
"indent": [2, 2]
```

Incorrect error:

```
t.js:1:15: Expected indentation of 2 characters.
```

rename.from: indent rule false positive in "switch" statement

body: what was the config used for the rule?

This rule is reporting incorrectly because you dont have `;` at the end of returns.
I will further investigate whats going on here.

I think this maybe an issue with Espree.
Switch case node has an line start of 3 and line end of 4. when the statements dont have `;` at the end.

But I checked [esprima](http://esprima.org/demo/parse.html?code=function%20test%28%29%7B%0Aswitch%28a%29%20%7B%0A%20%20%20%20case%20%22a%22%3A%20return%20console.log%28%22A%22%29%0A%20%20%20%20case%20%22b%22%3A%20return%20console.log%28%22B%22%29%0A%7D%0A%7D), it parses it correctly.

Issue logged to Espree: https://github.com/eslint/espree/issues/164
Once we fix the Espree issue, there is no change required on this rule.
Still can reproduce this bug on 1.0.0-rc-1
Hmmm... @lo1tuma added unittests to verify reported scenario. If yours differ, can you open a new issue?

@mistadikay was missing the indent case option.
https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/3024
